title: Message Cooldown Logger
prompt:
Implement a stateful `MessageCooldownLogger` for suppressing repeated log messages. `MessageCooldownLogger()` starts empty. `should_print(timestamp, message)` returns `True` when the message may be emitted and `False` when it must be suppressed.

Each message has an independent fixed cooldown of 10 seconds. A call is allowed when that message has never been allowed before, or when `timestamp - last_allowed_timestamp >= 10`. Record the timestamp only for an allowed call; a suppressed call must not extend the cooldown.

Timestamps are non-negative integers supplied in nondecreasing order across all calls. Messages are non-empty strings. Use expected O(1) time per call and O(number of distinct messages) state.

example.input: logger = MessageCooldownLogger(); [logger.should_print(t, m) for t, m in [(1, 'sync'), (4, 'sync'), (11, 'sync')]]
example.reasoning: The event at time 4 is suppressed, while the event at time 11 is exactly ten seconds after the last allowed event.
